summary: Forest Service lookout site on Stahl Peak (Stahl Mountain), Lewis County, WA: L-4 cab built 1933, gone by 1956; photos show only the former cab site and anchor bolts.

facts.status_note: Cab gone by 1956. WillhiteWeb photos show the site of the former cab with anchor bolts; no source describes a structure standing today.

access.note: Route described in a hiking guide: a gravel road from FR 74 and FR 7409, then an unsigned trail on National Forest land. The sources read name no closure or permit requirement.

visit.trail_note: Drive from Highway 7 along FR 74 and FR 7409 for about seven miles, then walk 0.75 miles one way on an unsigned trail. Nothing stands to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forests per the register; Gifford Pinchot National Forest per firelookout.com; Snoqualmie National Forest per the Forest Lookouts list. The story reports all three; no source settles it.

notes_for_editor: Only four sources were read. None gives a removal date beyond gone by 1956, and the Forest Lookouts page says only Removed. The national forest is disputed three ways, and the story says so. The 1934 telephone line year comes from a February 1934 item that gives January 15 as the completion date. No staffing or fire information was found, so none is recorded. The public access level rests on WillhiteWeb's route description and on no closure being named in the sources read; it is not confirmed by a Forest Service page. The brief's other_names entry (Stahl Mountain) is supported by WillhiteWeb and Forest Lookouts.
